video_title: Doug Christie addresses Kings' margin for error, turnovers | NBC Sports California

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Kings' first-quarter struggles against defensive blitzing
quotes.excerpt: they started blitzing Darius and trying to take him out of the game
quotes.quote: Getting off in the first quarter, I think we tried to play some toss, some splits because they started blitzing Darius and trying to take him out of the game. Unfortunately, E-Man got into a little bit of foul trouble there early on. After that first quarter, which was a blitz, that second and third quarter was more along the lines, but we got to bottle up that and figure out a way to get that for 48 minutes. That's the key.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie on the Kings' first quarter struggles against the blitz: We have to bottle up that second and third quarter intensity and figure out a way to get that for 48 minutes.

structured.context: Assistant coach Doug Christie discusses the Kings' struggles against defensive blitzing directed at Darius Garland.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Need for better offensive spacing against defensive pressure
quotes.excerpt: you need three outlets when they're going to blitz Darius
quotes.quote: You need three outlets when they're going to blitz Darius. It's the roller who's setting the screen, somebody has to come up out of the corner. I think we were a little late on everything in that first half, even on the rotations. We have to be aggressive. It's something that we went over in practice, it's something that we looked at in film and talked to them about, but you got to give them credit. They've won championships, they know exactly what they want to do.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie says the Kings need better spacing and three outlets when teams blitz Darius. He admits they were a little late on rotations in the first half.

structured.context: Doug Christie explains the necessary offensive adjustments and spacing required to counter defensive pressure on Darius Garland.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: High turnover rate is unsustainable for Kings
quotes.excerpt: 20 turnovers for 26 points is never going to do it
quotes.quote: We have to take care of the basketball at a really, really high level because our margin for error is not huge, but 20 turnovers for 26 points is never going to do it. We got to take care of that basketball.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie on the Kings' turnover issues: Our margin for error is not huge, but 20 turnovers for 26 points is never going to do it. We have to take care of the basketball.

structured.context: Doug Christie addresses the team's high turnover rate and the need for better ball security.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Darius will face more defensive variety moving forward
quotes.excerpt: Darius is going to continue to see every defense that that you can create
quotes.quote: I think you're going to see it more. I think Darius is going to continue to see every defense that that you can create. They were blitzing small-small, they were blitzing small-big, so it didn't matter. If it was a five-man they were blitzing, if it was a small they were blitzing. I think probably haven't seen the small-small blitz, but even that goes for not only Darius, but it goes for the screener. Where are you going once that happens? You got to release and find an area that he can pass you the basketball, coming up out of the corner.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie expects Darius to keep seeing heavy defensive pressure: Darius is going to continue to see every defense that you can create. It is about finding the right spots once the blitz happens.

structured.context: Doug Christie predicts that Darius Garland will continue to face varied defensive blitzing schemes from opponents.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: E-Man's physical style and rookie learning curve
quotes.excerpt: E-Man, he plays a physical style of basketball and I tell him to don't back up
quotes.quote: E-Man, he plays a physical style of basketball and I tell him to don't back up. But trying to work with him, talk with him about what he's going to see on a night-to-night basis and what the referees are going to be calling. Unfortunately, he got his second and then later in the second half, I believe he got his fourth, so it was just kind of seeing how far we were going to go with him. Love what he brings, love all of the intangibles that he brings to the game. It's, being a rookie, you got to learn the flow of the game and how to survive out there without getting yourself in foul trouble.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie on rookie E-Man: I love what he brings and all the intangibles, but he has to learn the flow of the game and how to survive out there without getting himself in foul trouble.

structured.context: Doug Christie discusses the physical playstyle of rookie E-Man and the challenges of avoiding foul trouble.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Focusing on controllable factors to improve performance
quotes.excerpt: talking about the things that that we can control
quotes.quote: More than anything, just talking about the things that that we can control. Not turning the basketball over, making sure to Sean's point, making ourselves available when they begin to blitz us. Playing with a more sense of urgency as far as pace, getting into our stuff quicker so that we're not deeper into the shot clock and all of a sudden you're finding yourself in butter clock, which is seven or under and you're rushing shots. The quicker we can get into it, and then obviously getting defensive stops and getting out and running.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie says the Kings need to play with more urgency: We have to get into our stuff quicker so we are not deeper into the shot clock and finding ourselves rushing shots.

structured.context: Doug Christie outlines the controllable factors the team must focus on to improve their offensive pace and execution.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Kings' pride and resilience despite the deficit
quotes.excerpt: this group has a lot of pride in what they do and they're going to continue to fight
quotes.quote: I know that the one thing is this group has a lot of pride in what they do and they're going to continue to fight. When you're down like that and you you get it back to four, eight, 10, it's about getting over the hump. And if you don't, then all of a sudden you you might go, ah. Or they made some they made some big shots. I think there was a bank three, a couple last-second shots that went in, back doors. Those are things that we talked about, make sure that push everything up the floor, no back doors. But, you know, Draymond has has run that offense for the number of years at a really, really high level, so if you make a mistake, he's going to make you pay for it.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie on the Kings' resilience: This group has a lot of pride and they are going to continue to fight, but if you make a mistake against Draymond, he is going to make you pay for it.

structured.context: Doug Christie reflects on the team's resilience and the difficulty of defending against Draymond Green's offensive playmaking.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: DeAnthony Melton's defensive lapse and rebounding emphasis
quotes.excerpt: I think he leaked out. I don't think it was anything that guys didn't do
quotes.quote: I think he leaked out. I don't think it was anything that guys didn't do. He just leaked out. Everyone's looking at the basketball trying to rebound, offensive rebound, because we wanted to crash and make sure that we were emphasizing that. That's an area we wanted to get at least 15, we got 12 of them tonight. But he got behind the defense and they just threw it long.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie explains a defensive lapse: We wanted to crash the glass and emphasize offensive rebounding, but DeAnthony Melton leaked out and they just threw it long.

structured.context: Doug Christie explains a specific defensive breakdown involving DeAnthony Melton during a rebounding attempt.
